items.quote: System cooldown: ~ 60 hours from room temperature to 4 K (varies with different magnet options)
items.document_title: TeslatronPT product page (Oxford Instruments Nanoscience Japan, archived 2021)
items.note: Oxford Instruments (original maker of the TeslatronPT; product line now Quantum Design Oxford) spec, archived product page: system cooldown ~60 h from room temperature to 4 K, covering the 8/12/14 T and 6/1/1 T magnet options (manufacturer notes it varies with magnet option). The same figure appears in the archived Oxford Instruments TeslatronPT brochure (research/v5/cache/0e5c60155807730b.txt, 'System cooldown 60 hours from room temperature to 4 K'). The current QD-Oxford documents give only the sample-probe cooldown (< 2 h into a cold VTI), which is cooldown_time.sample_exchange, not this value.

No source states a cooling time from room temperature to -190 C for the TTK 600 with LN2 cooling. The Malvern Panalytical/Anton Paar leaflet (research/v5/cache/99e0b6b2037d93a3.txt) gives only ranges; the Anton Paar product pages return HTTP 403 to the snapshot tool, and web searches turned up no manual or datasheet with a cooldown or cooling-rate figure.
Same instrument as anton_paar_ttk600_ln2_vacuum: no documented cooldown time to -190 C was found in the leaflet, the product pages (HTTP 403) or web searches.

The ILL equipment card for 82ILHV100, the ILL Orange instruction manual and the ILL history page give no cooldown time to base (only fill steps, e.g. 'Normally 12 litres of liquid helium are sufficient to cool down and fill the bath'). Lead that was not applied: NIST's facility page for its own 100 mm Orange cryostat OC-100 (snapshot c2abc65056a27b39) lists 'Cooldown to Base Temp. ~4 hrs.' after a > 4 h vacuum-jacket pump-out and a ~40 min LHe fill. That is a different physical unit at another facility, not a manufacturer specification for the ILL unit, so it is not reported as this configuration's value.

items.quote: initial cool down time of system without insert (unattended) | 15 .. 20 h (system without magnet), 20 .. 24 h (incl. 9 T magnet)
items.note: attocube spec: initial cooldown of the system with the 9 T magnet is 20-24 h (upper bound 24 h), stated for the system without insert. The datasheet separately gives 'cool down time of sample approx. 3 .. 5 h (depending on insert)'; that insert/sample step is not included in this value. Same figures in the attoDRY2100 datasheet PDF (research/v5/cache/465c82dd2b1ea577.txt). This configuration uses the attoCFM I insert; its insert cooldown (3-5 h) comes on top of this value.

items.quote: Cooling down time from 180°C to -40°C | 110 min
items.document_title: Model MK 240 (BINDER product page, technical specifications)
items.location: Technical specifications, Performance Data Temperature, MK240-400V (9020-0376)
items.note: BINDER's documented pull-down time to the minimum set point (-40 C, the configuration's base temperature), measured from 180 C rather than from room temperature. BINDER gives no room-temperature-to--40 C figure. Because cooling from 180 C passes through room temperature, 110 min is the documented upper bound used here.

items.quote: Cooling down time from 180°C to -70°C | 110 min
items.document_title: Model MKFT 240 (BINDER product page, technical specifications)
items.note: BINDER's documented pull-down time to the minimum set point (-70 C, the configuration's base temperature), measured from 180 C rather than from room temperature. BINDER gives no room-temperature figure. Because cooling from 180 C passes through room temperature, 110 min is the documented upper bound used here.

The Bluefors product page (snapshot b3667c5f30dc8b2b) shows cooldown curves only as a graphic with no stated number, and gives 'Wafer exchange time (measurement-to-measurement) | ~ 3 h', which is a load-lock wafer swap with the system cold, not a cooldown from room temperature. The AEM-Afore co-developer page gives no cooldown time either, and web searches found no manufacturer or paper figure for this model.
